entities.summary:
Unas or Wenis, also spelled Unis, was a king, the ninth and last ruler of the Fifth Dynasty of Egypt during the Old Kingdom. Unas reigned for around 30 years in the mid-24th century BC, succeeding Djedkare Isesi, who might have been his father.

Unas is notable for being one of the few Egyptian pharaohs whose tomb was discovered intact, providing valuable insights into the culture and architecture of the Old Kingdom. The discovery of Unas' tomb, KV47, has shed light on the construction techniques and artistic styles of the period.

Despite his significant contributions to the history of ancient Egypt, Unas is often overshadowed by more famous pharaohs of the Old Kingdom, such as Khufu and Khafre. Nevertheless, Unas' legacy continues to fascinate historians and archaeologists, offering a unique window into the culture and politics of ancient Egypt.
